channel.description: Approved local stories in broadcast order

item.description: Gas prices in Vermont have dropped below four dollars per gallon, averaging three dollars and ninety-two cents. Burlington prices fell nearly twenty cents to three dollars and ninety cents per gallon. The national average is at its lowest since mid-March, just before Thanksgiving.

Quarry Valley School Board reviewed a second draft of its fiscal year twenty twenty-eight budget. Education spending is projected to rise by four point two percent, with health insurance premiums adjusted to a two point five percent increase. The board approved a ten thousand dollar capital improvement for Proctor schools and will meet again in December.

Vermont state employees will face a nine percent increase in health insurance premiums starting January first. This matches last year's increase after previous steep hikes. The state employees' union is urging Governor Phil Scott to cap hospital prices to lower costs.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul announced student loan relief programs for nurses and farmers. The programs offer two point one million dollars in forgiveness. Applications are open until December sixteenth, twenty twenty-six.
